newsitem.title: UK: Euro will be top bond issuance currency - IPMA/ISMA.
newsitem.headline: Euro will be top bond issuance currency - IPMA/ISMA.

text.p: Europe's single currency, the euro, is expected to rival the dollar as the major international bond issuance currency, representatives from bond industry bodies said on Tuesday.

"IPMA's current agenda is dominated by the issue of European monetary union and the creation of the euro," Robert Gray, vice chairman of the International Primary Markets Association (IPMA) and chairman of HSBC Markets said at a capital markets conference.
"The euro will rival the dollar as the currency most frequently used by international borrowers and investors," he said.

Professor Brian Scott-Quinn, director of the International Securities Market Association (ISMA) Centre at Britain's Reading University, said: "The euro securities market will rival the dollar, and also the yen, markets."
Last year, over $670 billion was raised on the international bond markets, Capital DATA Bondware figures showed, and dollar issuance accounted for 41 percent of the total.
But the adoption of common market practices across Europe, such as day count conventions and settlement periods, was crucial in the development of the euro sector.
"The euro market will be divided by the current different national practices, conventions and standards," Scott-Quinn said.
"The existence of these (differences) for similar euro-denominated instruments might result in confusion, particularly for non-sovereign issues," he said.
Borrowers have already started preparing for European economic and monetary union (EMU).

At the start of this year a flurry of so-called parallel bonds were launched in core EMU currencies. The deals redenominate into the euro, due to be introduced on January 1, 1999 when the third phase EMU kicks in, and are fungible with each other, thus ensuring liquidity.
So far some European sovereigns, the European Investment Bank (EIB) and European borrowers like L-Bank and Siemens have tapped this market.
In the pipeline is a deal for Brazil, and borrowers like Japan-guaranteed Japan Finance Corp for Municipal Enterprises (JFM) were also said to be eyeing the market.

"Our market is already gearing up for the arrival of the euro, the best example is the parallel bond," Gray said, adding such transaction would lead to the gradual adoption of a euro mentality among issuers and investors.
In the first quarter of the 1997, the market saw over $10 billion equivalent of euro-related bond issues, Capital DATA Bondware said, a 5.4 percent market share.
